guide.title: Brent, London: Wembley Stadium, the OVO Arena, Old St Andrew's Kingsbury and the Welsh Harp
guide.intro: Brent is an outer London borough north-west of the centre, and it reads as four places rather than one. Wembley Park holds the 90,000-seat national stadium under its 134-metre arch, with the 1934 Empire Pool beside it. Kilburn, Queen's Park and Brondesbury run along the Camden and Westminster boundaries, with an Art Deco cinema seating 4,004 on the High Road, a producing theatre further along the same road, a City of London Corporation park with an 1891 bandstand and a cemetery of 1855. Willesden, Harlesden and Neasden hold the medieval church of the old Middlesex parish, a Hindu mandir inaugurated in 1995, a Jewish cemetery in use since 1873 and the borough museum. Kingsbury, the Welsh Harp and Sudbury keep 103 hectares of countryside at Fryent, a reservoir and a Charles Holden station of 1931. The National Heritage List for England records 95 listed-building entries inside the Brent boundary as mapped by OpenStreetMap relation 75767.

sections.heading: Wembley Park and Wembley
sections.body:
Three buildings carry this quarter. Wembley Stadium, HA9 0WS, seats 90,000 and opened in 2007 on the site of the stadium that stood from 1923 until 2000. It is crowned by the 134-metre (440 ft) Wembley Arch, which supports over 75 per cent of the roof load, and two partially retractable roof structures over the east and west ends can be opened to let sunlight onto the pitch. Populous and Foster and Partners designed it, Multiplex built it, and the cost was 798 million pounds. The Football Association owns the ground through its subsidiary Wembley National Stadium Ltd, and it hosts most England home matches and the FA Cup Final. Entry is by event ticket or by booked stadium tour, and the operator publishes no tour times or prices, so none are given here. The ground carries no entry on the National Heritage List for England.

The OVO Arena Wembley stands on Arena Square off Engineers Way, HA9 0AA, 471 m from Wembley Stadium rail station and 609 m from Wembley Park Underground station. The operator states that the venue was originally opened as the Empire Pool in July 1934, built for the 1934 British Empire Games, and gives the capacity as 12,500, with over 120 shows a year and over a million visitors. It held boxing, diving, swimming and water polo at the 1948 Summer Olympics and badminton and rhythmic gymnastics at the 2012 Summer Olympics, and its first concert was in 1959. Legends Global manages and operates it. The building is listed Grade II as WEMBLEY ARENA (FORMERLY THE EMPIRE POOL), NHLE 1078877, on 14 October 1976.

Brent Town Hall stands on Forty Lane, HA9 9LY, in Barnhill ward, and is listed Grade II, NHLE 1262141, on 24 September 1990. It is T-shaped, with a long facade on Forty Lane. Built as Wembley Town Hall, it was the seat of Brent Council until 2013 and is now occupied by the Lycee International de Londres Winston Churchill, so the visit is a look at the facade from Forty Lane rather than a way in. Wikidata holds the building as Q4961570 and gives its administrative unit as the London Borough of Brent.

sections.heading: Kilburn, Queen's Park and Brondesbury
sections.body:
Kilburn High Road runs along the Brent side of the boundary with Camden, and two of the borough's performance buildings stand on it. The Gaumont State Cinema, 197-199 Kilburn High Road, NW6 7HY, is listed Grade II*, NHLE 1078889, on 10 October 1980, under the name Mecca Bingo, its use at the date of listing. George Coles designed it, it seated 4,004, and its 120 ft (37 m) tower is modelled on the Empire State Building and gave the building the name State. It is in use as Ruach City Church rather than as a general-admission attraction, and the frontage and tower are in view from the High Road. Brondesbury on the Mildmay line is 551 m away, Kilburn High Road on the Lioness line 575 m and Kilburn Park on the Bakerloo line 719 m.

Kiln Theatre is further along the same road at number 269, NW6 7JR, and stages plays and cinema screenings; the box office is on 020 7328 1000. The operator's own history records a Foresters' meeting hall of 1929, converted to a theatre in 1980 by Shirley Barrie and Ken Chubb, who named it the Tricycle Theatre after their Wakefield Tricycle Company, and the building re-opened as Kiln Theatre in September 2018. Nicolas Kent became artistic director in 1984, Indhu Rubasingham joined in 2012 and Amit Sharma became artistic director in 2023. The theatre has produced original work by Zadie Smith, Lynn Nottage, Roy Williams, Moira Buffini, Abi Morgan and Florian Zeller. Brondesbury is 289 m from the theatre's postcode and Kilburn on the Jubilee line 551 m.

Queen's Park, off Kingswood Avenue, NW6 6SG, is owned and managed by the City of London Corporation, one of the Corporation's green spaces outside the City. Entry is free, and the Corporation gives the remaining public expanse as 30 acres. It states that the park was established in 1879 to host the Royal Agricultural Society's International Exhibition, and that Alexander McKenzie, also the designer of the Alexandra Palace grounds and bailiff of Epping Forest and Burnham Beeches, produced the layout in 1887. The bandstand of 1891, cast in iron by Macfarlane and Co. of Glasgow and restored in 1992, is listed Grade II, NHLE 1382063, on 16 August 2000, and a K6 telephone kiosk at the Milman Road entrance is listed Grade II, NHLE 1078891. A Lych Gate of 1936, built to mark King George V's Coronation Jubilee, survives as a seating area in the Quiet Garden. There are tennis courts, a pitch and putt course, an ornamental garden, a children's playground with a sandpit, a small farm and a cafe; cycling is not permitted under the byelaws, and the Corporation warns that the park may close at short notice when wind speeds are forecast at 40 mph or above. Queens Park rail station is 209 m from the Kingswood Avenue address and Queen's Park Underground station 238 m.

Paddington Old Cemetery, on Willesden Lane, NW6 7SD, opened in 1855 and is a working municipal cemetery managed by Brent Council. It is a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1001542, recorded by Historic England at 10.07 hectares, and it carries an old Westminster parish's name while standing in Brent, in Queens Park ward. The mortuary chapels are separately listed Grade II as THE CHAPELS AT PADDINGTON CEMETERY, NHLE 1359002, on 27 May 1982, and the grave of the painter Sigismund Goetze is listed Grade II in its own right, NHLE 1389534, on 8 November 2001. The council warns that extra safety measures are in place around the chapels while structural investigations take place, so the chapels may not be approachable. It opens every day including bank holidays, 9am to 4pm from January to February and from November to December, 9am to 6pm in March, 9am to 7pm in April and September, 9am to 8pm from May to August and 9am to 5pm in October, with last entry 15 minutes before closing. Brondesbury Park is 400 m from the chapels and Queen's Park 540 m.

sections.heading: Willesden, Harlesden and Neasden
sections.body:
This is the old Middlesex parish core and the industrial suburbs west of it, and it holds six of the borough's places. St Mary's Church, on Neasden Lane, NW10 2TS, is listed Grade II* as CHURCH OF ST MARY, NHLE 1359036, on 26 July 1951. There has been a church on the site since 938; the present building dates from the 13th century, with restorations in 1850, 1872 and 1893. A shrine to Our Lady of Willesden existed from the 13th century, was destroyed at the Reformation and was restored at the beginning of the 20th century. The Roman Catholic Church of Our Lady of Willesden, a separate building, is listed Grade II, NHLE 1064217, on 15 March 1979, and St Matthew's Church, built between 1900 and 1906 to designs by W. D. Caroe, stands about 900 m south and is listed Grade II, NHLE 1359020. Neasden on the Jubilee line is 558 m from St Mary's and Dollis Hill 762 m.

The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, 105-119 Brentfield Road, NW10 8LD, was inaugurated in 1995 by Pramukh Swami Maharaj and belongs to the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha. It was built entirely by traditional methods and in traditional materials, in stone rather than in a converted secular building, and the complex holds a permanent exhibition, Understanding Hinduism, and a cultural centre with an assembly hall, gymnasium, bookshop and offices. The operator states that the Mandir and Haveli are usually open to the public from 9.00am to 6.00pm throughout the year, including Bank Holidays, and gives the same timings for the exhibition; entry to the mandir is free. Neasden is 1,048 m away and Stonebridge Park 1,142 m, so every approach is a walk of over a kilometre. The site carries no entry on the National Heritage List for England.

Willesden Jewish Cemetery, which runs a heritage centre under the name House of Life, is on Beaconsfield Road, NW10 2JE, and is a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1449184, recorded by Historic England at 8.04 hectares. The operator states that nearly 30,000 men, women and children have been buried here since 1873, and Wikipedia gives 29,800 graves. Nathan Rothschild, 1st Baron Rothschild, and members of his family are buried here, and the tomb of Rosalind Franklin, co-discoverer of the structure of DNA, is listed Grade II, NHLE 1444176, on 7 March 2017. Four monuments inside the cemetery carry their own Grade II listings: the complex of funerary buildings, NHLE 1448718, on 1 August 2017; the burial enclosures of Mayer, Juliana and Hannah Rothschild, NHLE 1449844; the tomb of Max Eberstadt, NHLE 1449845; and the war memorial of 1961 by Ralph Hobday, NHLE 1449842, the last three all on 5 September 2017. The House of Life project, funded by a National Lottery Heritage Fund grant of 2015, opened the cemetery to visitors on 7 September 2020. Dollis Hill is 485 m from the Beaconsfield Road postcode.

Roundwood Park, on Harlesden Road, NW10 3SH, is free, managed by Brent Council and a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1001556, recorded by Historic England at 10.63 hectares. The council describes a formal Victorian park and names an aviary, a cafe, a children's playground, a picnic area with tables, a public toilet, a sports hall, sports pitches and courts, a wildlife area, bowling greens taken by booking, multi-use games areas and outdoor gyms; a dog control order applies to the entrance and flower garden areas. The ground was known in the 19th century as Knowles Hill or Hunger Hill Common Field, and the present name comes from Roundwood House, which stood beside it. Wikipedia names Oliver Claude Robson as the designer who created the park and gives the area as 26.5 acres. Nothing is within a kilometre: Willesden Junction is 1,081 m from the Harlesden Road address and Dollis Hill 1,228 m.

The Church of All Souls stands on the traffic island where Station Road meets Harlesden High Street, NW10 4UJ, and is listed Grade II*, NHLE 1359000, on 23 January 1974; Harlesden town centre grew around it. Wikidata holds it as Q17541751 and gives the London Borough of Brent as its administrative unit. The Jubilee Clock in Harlesden is listed Grade II, NHLE 1359035, on 23 January 1974, and Wikipedia dates the clock tower to 1888, marking Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee of 1887; the Green Man public house is listed Grade II, NHLE 1294638. Willesden Junction is the nearest station to the church, 367 m to the Lioness and Mildmay platforms and 399 m to the Bakerloo line, with Harlesden 684 m and 700 m.

Brent Museum and Archives occupies the second floor of The Library at Willesden Green, 95 High Road, NW10 2SF, and is free. The museum and exhibition space open Monday to Friday 10.30am to 8pm, Saturday 10.30am to 5pm and Sunday 12pm to 5pm; the archives open Tuesday to Thursday 10.30am to 5pm, to 8pm every alternate Thursday, Friday 11am to 4pm for volunteers and project partners only, and alternate Saturdays 10.30am to 5pm with a closure from 1pm to 2pm, and at least one week's notice is required for an archives appointment. It is the borough museum and record office combined, holding photographs, documents and objects of local history, and a current exhibition, Brent Records Album Covers, shows the covers of reggae albums released from the 1960s to the 2020s. Contact is museum.archives@brent.gov.uk and 020 8937 3600. Willesden Green station, 624 m from the library postcode, is itself listed Grade II, NHLE 1391808.

sections.heading: Kingsbury, the Welsh Harp and Sudbury
sections.body:
The north and west of the borough are its open country, and they hold its Grade I building. Old St Andrew's Church, on Old Church Lane, NW9 8TA, is listed Grade I as OLD PARISH CHURCH OF ST ANDREW, NHLE 1188676, on 6 October 1952; Brent holds one Grade I entry on the National Heritage List for England, and this is it. Wikidata holds it as Q7085063 and gives an inception of 1150. It is vested in the Churches Conservation Trust, which states that access is available by appointment only, by contacting Father Ioan Sarpe, and a Romanian Orthodox congregation uses it under a twenty-year lease from 2012; the vesting dates from 7 October 2010. A second church stands in the same churchyard, the New Parish Church of St Andrew, listed Grade II*, NHLE 1078874, on 6 October 1952, moved here from Wells Street in Marylebone, and six churchyard monuments are listed Grade II in their own right on 18 November 1996: the chest tomb to Joseph Finch, NHLE 1267872, the monument to William Frederick Ashton, NHLE 1267871, and the tombstones to Edwin Austin Abbey, NHLE 1267873, Henry Wetherilt, NHLE 1267869, Thomas Raworth, NHLE 1267875, and Timothy Wetherilt, NHLE 1267866. Wembley Park, 1,398 m away, is the single station within 1,500 m, and the Trust gives the same figure as 0.8 miles.

Brent Reservoir, known as the Welsh Harp, is reached from Birchen Grove: NW9 7LY for the Welsh Harp Open Space and NW9 8RY for the Welsh Harp Environmental Education Centre. The open space and towpaths are free. Brent Council describes 170 hectares of open water, marshes, trees and grassland and states that it is a Site of Special Scientific Interest; Wikipedia gives the Site of Special Scientific Interest as 68.6 hectares, or 170 acres. The water straddles the Brent-Barnet boundary, is owned by the Canal & River Trust, is fed by the Silk Stream and the River Brent and holds an estimated 1,600,000 cubic metres. The name comes from a public house, The Welsh Harp, which stood nearby until the early 1970s. The open space came into existence in 1965 and lies north-west of the water, and the education centre sits in 15 acres of woodland and has been managed by the waterways charity Thames21 since 2016. Sailing clubs on the water include Welsh Harp Sailing Club, Wembley Sailing Club, the Sea Cadets and the University of London sailing club, and fishing is prohibited. The two bird hides are locked and the council directs visitors to the education centre for access. A Site of Special Scientific Interest is a Natural England designation, and the reservoir carries no entry on the National Heritage List for England.

Fryent Country Park covers 103 hectares of traditional Middlesex countryside off Fryent Way, NW9 9SE, in the council's own words, and is free. Barn Hill, the high point, rises to 86 m and is capped by pebble gravel, Gotfords Hill reaches 63 m and Beane Hill 65 m, and the rest of the park lies on London clay. Fryent Way bisects it, the Capital Ring footpath passes through it, part is let on licence for the grazing of ponies and there is no formal organised sport. There is a rough-surfaced car park for about 50 vehicles on the western side of Fryent Way. Wikipedia gives 103 hectares (254 acres) for the park with Barn Hill Open Space together. It is a nature reserve, classed as Metropolitan Open Land and as a wildlife site of Metropolitan Importance under the system Brent and the Greater London Authority use, and it carries no entry on the National Heritage List for England. Kingsbury on the Jubilee line is 539 m from the Fryent Way address and the single station within 1,200 m of it.

Sudbury Town Underground Station, on Station Approach, HA0 2LA, is listed Grade II*, NHLE 1294594, on 19 February 1971, and Wikidata holds it as Q1768993 and gives Charles Holden as the architect. It is a working station on the Uxbridge branch of the Piccadilly line, between Sudbury Hill and Alperton, in fare zone 4, and the ticket hall can be seen without admission; the forecourt is known as Station Crescent. The main entrance on Station Approach is in Brent, on the boundary the station shares with Ealing. Sudbury & Harrow Road on Chiltern Railways is 491 m away and Wembley Central about 1.3 km east. A K8 telephone kiosk at Northwick Park station is listed Grade II, NHLE 1485378, on 9 June 2023.

Barham Park, at 660 Harrow Road, HA0 2HB, is free, managed by Brent Council and has free parking on site for about 16 cars. The council describes a gently undulating park with pathways and many mature trees that has maintained much of its formal Victorian character, and calls the walled garden a popular relaxation spot with visitors; a dog control order applies to the walled garden. The park and several local landmarks take their name from the Barham family, formerly major landowners in Sudbury. The surviving structures of Barham Old Court - garden walls, gates, a pergola of two Portland stone Ionic columns and a sundial on Portland stone Ionic columns - are listed Grade II, NHLE 1294729, on 15 March 1979, while the park itself is not on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. Wembley Fire Station, on Harrow Road, is listed Grade II, NHLE 1247236, on 24 November 2000, and the Grade II* Hundred Elms Farm outbuilding, NHLE 1078876, listed 6 October 1952, stands 1,087 m north-west at Dyson Court, HA0 2NZ. Sudbury Town Underground station is 354 m from the park and Sudbury & Harrow Road 408 m.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Brent is served by four Underground lines - the Jubilee, the Metropolitan, the Bakerloo and the Piccadilly - by two Overground lines, the Lioness and the Mildmay, and by National Rail, with Chiltern Railways to Wembley Stadium and to Sudbury & Harrow Road and Southern to Wembley Central. There is no Elizabeth line station, no DLR and no tram in the borough. The Lioness line is the Watford DC route through Kensal Green, Queens Park, Kilburn High Road, Willesden Junction, Harlesden, Stonebridge Park and Wembley Central; the Mildmay line is the North London route through Kensal Rise, Brondesbury Park and Brondesbury. Willesden Junction, Wembley Central, Queen's Park, Kensal Green, Stonebridge Park and Harlesden each have both an Underground stop and an Overground or National Rail stop, with separate Naptan identifiers.

Wembley Park, on the Jubilee and Metropolitan lines, is the year-round station for the stadium and the arena: 801 m from Wembley Stadium and 609 m from the OVO Arena Wembley. Wembley Stadium rail station, 490 m from the ground, is served by Chiltern Railways and opens for events. Three stations in the borough are themselves listed: Willesden Green, on the Jubilee and Metropolitan lines, Grade II, NHLE 1391808; Kilburn Park on the Bakerloo line, by Stanley Heaps, Grade II, NHLE 1078871; and Sudbury Town on the Piccadilly line, Grade II*, NHLE 1294594.

Distances are longer in the north and west. Kingsbury on the Jubilee line is 539 m from Fryent Country Park and the single station within 1,200 m of it. Wembley Park is 1,398 m from Old St Andrew's Church, Kingsbury, and the single station within 1,500 m. From Birchen Grove, NW9 8RY, at the Welsh Harp Environmental Education Centre, Wembley Park is 1,531 m and Neasden 1,555 m, both in Brent, while Hendon is 1,975 m and Brent Cross West 2,255 m, both in Barnet; from the Welsh Harp Open Space address, NW9 7LY, Hendon on Thameslink is nearest at 1,414 m. Roundwood Park and the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir each stand more than a kilometre from any station, at 1,081 m and 1,048 m respectively.

faq.question: What are the opening hours at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden?
faq.answer: The operator states that the Mandir and Haveli are usually open to the public from 9.00am to 6.00pm throughout the year, including Bank Holidays, and gives the same timings for the Understanding Hinduism exhibition. Entry to the mandir is free. The address is 105-119 Brentfield Road, NW10 8LD. Neasden on the Jubilee line is 1,048 m away, Stonebridge Park 1,142 m on the Lioness line and 1,151 m on the Bakerloo line, and Harlesden about 1.2 km, so every approach is a walk of over a kilometre.

faq.question: Which Brent sites publish opening hours, and which do not?
faq.answer: Four do. The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir opens 9.00am to 6.00pm year-round; Brent Museum and Archives opens Monday to Friday 10.30am to 8pm, Saturday 10.30am to 5pm and Sunday 12pm to 5pm, with narrower archive hours; the Willesden Jewish Cemetery heritage centre opens Sunday 10:00 to 16:00 and Monday to Thursday 10:00 to 13:00; and Brent Council publishes month-by-month times for Paddington Old Cemetery. Wembley Stadium tours, the OVO Arena and the council's park pages for Roundwood Park, Barham Park, Fryent Country Park and the Welsh Harp publish no opening hours, so none are given here.

faq.question: How do I reach Wembley Stadium and the OVO Arena Wembley?
faq.answer: Wembley Park, on the Jubilee and Metropolitan lines, is the year-round station for both: 801 m from Wembley Stadium, HA9 0WS, and 609 m from the OVO Arena Wembley, HA9 0AA. Wembley Stadium rail station is 490 m from the ground and 471 m from the arena, is served by Chiltern Railways and opens for events. Wembley Central, 1,274 m from the stadium, carries the Bakerloo line, the Lioness line and Southern services. The stadium is entered on event days by ticket or by booked tour; the arena admits ticket holders to events only.

faq.question: How many listed buildings does Brent hold?
faq.answer: The National Heritage List for England records 95 listed-building entries inside the Brent boundary as mapped by OpenStreetMap relation 75767: 1 at Grade I, 8 at Grade II* and 86 at Grade II. The unit is list entries rather than buildings, because a single entry can cover a whole terrace; Brent Council states one Grade I, nine Grade II* and around 200 Grade II buildings. The Grade I entry is Old St Andrew's Church, Kingsbury, NHLE 1188676. The borough also holds three Grade II registered parks and gardens and no scheduled monuments.

faq.question: Can I go inside Old St Andrew's Church, Kingsbury?
faq.answer: By appointment. The church, on Old Church Lane, NW9 8TA, is vested in the Churches Conservation Trust, which states that access is available by appointment only, by contacting Father Ioan Sarpe; a Romanian Orthodox congregation uses the building under a twenty-year lease from 2012. It is listed Grade I as OLD PARISH CHURCH OF ST ANDREW, NHLE 1188676, on 6 October 1952, and Wikidata gives an inception of 1150. Wembley Park, 1,398 m away, is the single station within 1,500 m of it.

faq.question: Which Brent parks and green spaces carry a designation?
faq.answer: Three are Grade II registered parks and gardens: Paddington Old Cemetery, NHLE 1001542, at 10.07 hectares; Roundwood Park, NHLE 1001556, at 10.63 hectares; and Willesden Jewish Cemetery, NHLE 1449184, at 8.04 hectares. Queen's Park is not on the register, though its 1891 bandstand is listed Grade II, NHLE 1382063, and a K6 kiosk at the Milman Road entrance Grade II, NHLE 1078891. At Barham Park the Barham Old Court walls, gates, pergola and sundial are listed Grade II, NHLE 1294729. Brent Reservoir is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, a Natural England designation with no entry on the National Heritage List for England.

photos.title: Wembley Stadium and its arch, seen from Olympic Way, Wembley Park
photos.description: The stadium fills the end of Olympic Way, its curved glazed frontage and banded roof truss rising above the Olympic Steps, with the steel lattice arch springing clear of the roofline against a pale overcast sky. Tall lighting masts and apartment blocks line the paved approach, and people are walking towards the entrance concourse.
photos.author: Hullian111

The mortuary chapels are separately listed Grade II as THE CHAPELS AT PADDINGTON CEMETERY, NHLE 1359002, on 27 May 1982, and the grave of the painter Sigismund Goetze is listed Grade II in its own right, NHLE 1389534, on 8 November 2001. Brondesbury Park is 400 m from the chapels, Queen's Park 540 m and Queens Park rail station 560 m.

places.name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
places.summary: The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir stands at 105-119 Brentfield Road, NW10 8LD. The operator states that the Mandir and Haveli are usually open to the public from 9.00am to 6.00pm throughout the year, including Bank Holidays, and gives the same timings for the Understanding Hinduism exhibition; entry to the mandir is free. Neasden on the Jubilee line is 1,048 m away and Stonebridge Park 1,142 m, so every approach is a walk of over a kilometre.
places.history: Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated the mandir in 1995, and it belongs to the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha. It was built entirely by traditional methods and in traditional materials, in stone rather than in a converted secular building. The complex holds a permanent exhibition, Understanding Hinduism, and a cultural centre with an assembly hall, gymnasium, bookshop and offices. The site carries no entry on the National Heritage List for England.

places.name: St Mary's Church, Willesden
places.address: St Mary's Church, Neasden Lane, Willesden, London NW10 2TS
places.summary: St Mary's Church stands on Neasden Lane, NW10 2TS, and is listed Grade II* as CHURCH OF ST MARY, NHLE 1359036, on 26 July 1951. It is a working Church of England parish church; the parish publishes no visitor hours, so none are given here, and service times are worth checking before travelling. Neasden on the Jubilee line is 558 m away and Dollis Hill 762 m.
places.history: There has been a church on the site since 938, and the present building dates from the 13th century, with restorations in 1850, 1872 and 1893. A shrine to Our Lady of Willesden existed from the 13th century, was destroyed at the Reformation and was restored at the beginning of the 20th century. The Roman Catholic Church of Our Lady of Willesden, a separate building, is listed Grade II, NHLE 1064217, on 15 March 1979, and St Matthew's Church, Willesden, built between 1900 and 1906 to designs by W. D. Caroe, stands about 900 m south and is listed Grade II, NHLE 1359020.

places.name: Willesden Jewish Cemetery (House of Life)
places.address: Willesden Jewish Cemetery, Beaconsfield Road, Willesden, London NW10 2JE
places.summary: Willesden Jewish Cemetery, which runs a heritage centre under the name House of Life, is on Beaconsfield Road, NW10 2JE, and is free to visit. It is a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1449184, recorded by Historic England at 8.04 hectares. The heritage centre and funerary buildings open Sunday 10:00 to 16:00 and Monday to Thursday 10:00 to 13:00 and are closed on Fridays; the grounds open Sunday to Thursday 8:00 to 17:00 in summer or 8:00 to 16:00 in winter, and Friday 8:00 to 17:00 in summer or 8:00 to 13:00 in winter, with the operator giving no date ranges for summer and winter. Saturdays, bank holidays and Jewish festivals are closed to both, and the operator warns that the heritage centre may close for events, private bookings or staff availability.
places.history: The operator states that nearly 30,000 men, women and children have been buried here since 1873, and Wikipedia gives 29,800 graves. Nathan Rothschild, 1st Baron Rothschild, and members of his family are buried here, and the tomb of Rosalind Franklin, co-discoverer of the structure of DNA, is listed Grade II, NHLE 1444176, on 7 March 2017. Four monuments inside the cemetery carry their own Grade II listings: the complex of funerary buildings, NHLE 1448718, on 1 August 2017; the burial enclosures of Mayer, Juliana and Hannah Rothschild, NHLE 1449844; the tomb of Max Eberstadt, NHLE 1449845; and the war memorial of 1961 by Ralph Hobday, NHLE 1449842, the last three all on 5 September 2017. The House of Life project, funded by a National Lottery Heritage Fund grant of 2015, opened the cemetery to visitors on 7 September 2020.

places.name: Roundwood Park
places.address: Roundwood Park, Harlesden Road, London NW10 3SH
places.summary: Roundwood Park, on Harlesden Road, NW10 3SH, is free and managed by Brent Council, and is a Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1001556, recorded by Historic England at 10.63 hectares. The council describes a formal Victorian park and names an aviary, a cafe, a children's playground, a picnic area with tables, a public toilet, a sports hall, sports pitches and courts, a wildlife area, bowling greens taken by booking, multi-use games areas and outdoor gyms; a dog control order applies to the entrance and flower garden areas. Nothing is within a kilometre: Willesden Junction is 1,081 m from the Harlesden Road address and Dollis Hill 1,228 m.
places.history: The ground was known in the 19th century as Knowles Hill or Hunger Hill Common Field, and the present name comes from Roundwood House, which stood beside it. Wikipedia names Oliver Claude Robson as the designer who created the park and gives the area as 26.5 acres, while Historic England records 10.63 hectares. The park has held the Green Flag Award.

places.name: Brent Museum and Archives
places.address: The Library at Willesden Green, second floor, 95 High Road, Willesden, London NW10 2SF
places.summary: Brent Museum and Archives occupies the second floor of The Library at Willesden Green, 95 High Road, NW10 2SF, and is free. The museum and exhibition space open Monday to Friday 10.30am to 8pm, Saturday 10.30am to 5pm and Sunday 12pm to 5pm. The archives open Tuesday to Thursday 10.30am to 5pm, to 8pm every alternate Thursday, Friday 11am to 4pm for volunteers and project partners only, and alternate Saturdays 10.30am to 5pm with a closure from 1pm to 2pm; at least one week's notice is required for an archives appointment. Willesden Green station is 624 m away.
places.history: It is the borough museum and record office combined, holding photographs, documents and objects of local history, and a current exhibition, Brent Records Album Covers, shows the covers of reggae albums released from the 1960s to the 2020s. It holds the photograph of the Queen's Park bandstand in 1905 that the City of London Corporation reproduces on its own history page. Contact is museum.archives@brent.gov.uk and 020 8937 3600. Willesden Green station, which serves it, is listed Grade II, NHLE 1391808.

places.name: Church of All Souls, Harlesden
places.address: All Souls Church, Station Road, Harlesden, London NW10 4UJ
places.summary: The Church of All Souls stands on the traffic island where Station Road meets Harlesden High Street, NW10 4UJ, and is listed Grade II*, NHLE 1359000, on 23 January 1974. It is a working parish church and publishes no visitor hours, so none are given here. Willesden Junction is the nearest station: 367 m to the Lioness and Mildmay platforms and 399 m to the Bakerloo line, with Harlesden 684 m and 700 m.
places.history: Harlesden town centre grew around the church, which stands at the junction of Station Road and Harlesden High Street. Wikidata holds it as Q17541751 and gives the London Borough of Brent as its administrative unit. The Jubilee Clock in Harlesden is listed Grade II, NHLE 1359035, on 23 January 1974, and Wikipedia dates the clock tower to 1888, marking Queen Victoria's Golden Jubilee of 1887; the Green Man public house is listed Grade II, NHLE 1294638.

places.name: Old St Andrew's Church, Kingsbury
places.address: Old St Andrew's Church, Old Church Lane, Kingsbury, London NW9 8TA
places.summary: Old St Andrew's Church, on Old Church Lane, NW9 8TA, is listed Grade I as OLD PARISH CHURCH OF ST ANDREW, NHLE 1188676, on 6 October 1952; Brent holds one Grade I entry on the National Heritage List for England, and this is it. The church is vested in the Churches Conservation Trust and used by a Romanian Orthodox congregation, and the Trust states that access is available by appointment only, by contacting Father Ioan Sarpe. Wembley Park, 1,398 m away, is the single station within 1,500 m, and the Trust gives the same figure as 0.8 miles.
places.history: Wikidata holds the church as Q7085063 and gives an inception of 1150. It was vested in the Churches Conservation Trust on 7 October 2010 and leased to the Romanian Orthodox Church for twenty years from 2012. A second church stands in the same churchyard, the New Parish Church of St Andrew, listed Grade II*, NHLE 1078874, on 6 October 1952, which was moved here from Wells Street in Marylebone. Six churchyard monuments are listed Grade II in their own right on 18 November 1996: the chest tomb to Joseph Finch, NHLE 1267872, the monument to William Frederick Ashton, NHLE 1267871, and the tombstones to Edwin Austin Abbey, NHLE 1267873, Henry Wetherilt, NHLE 1267869, Thomas Raworth, NHLE 1267875, and Timothy Wetherilt, NHLE 1267866.

places.name: Brent Reservoir (the Welsh Harp)
places.address: Welsh Harp Open Space, Birchen Grove, London NW9 7LY
places.summary: Brent Reservoir, known as the Welsh Harp, is reached from Birchen Grove: NW9 7LY for the Welsh Harp Open Space and NW9 8RY for the Welsh Harp Environmental Education Centre. The open space and towpaths are free. Brent Council describes 170 hectares of open water, marshes, trees and grassland and states that it is a Site of Special Scientific Interest; Wikipedia gives the Site of Special Scientific Interest as 68.6 hectares, or 170 acres. The two bird hides are locked, and the council directs visitors to the education centre for access.
places.history: The name comes from a public house, The Welsh Harp, which stood nearby until the early 1970s. The water straddles the Brent-Barnet boundary, is owned by the Canal & River Trust, is fed by the Silk Stream and the River Brent and holds an estimated 1,600,000 cubic metres. The Welsh Harp Open Space came into existence in 1965 and lies north-west of the water, and the Welsh Harp Environmental Education Centre sits in 15 acres of woodland and has been managed by the waterways charity Thames21 since 2016. Sailing clubs on the water include Welsh Harp Sailing Club, Wembley Sailing Club, the Sea Cadets and the University of London sailing club, and fishing is prohibited. A Site of Special Scientific Interest is a Natural England designation, and the reservoir carries no entry on the National Heritage List for England.

places.name: Fryent Country Park
places.address: Fryent Country Park, Fryent Way, London NW9 9SE
places.summary: Fryent Country Park covers 103 hectares of traditional Middlesex countryside off Fryent Way, NW9 9SE, in the council's own words, and is free. There is a rough-surfaced car park for about 50 vehicles on the western side of Fryent Way. Kingsbury on the Jubilee line is 539 m from the Fryent Way address and the single station within 1,200 m of it. The council publishes no opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: Barn Hill, the high point of the park, rises to 86 m and is capped by pebble gravel; Gotfords Hill reaches 63 m and Beane Hill 65 m, and the rest lies on London clay. Fryent Way bisects the park and the Capital Ring footpath passes through it. Part of the ground is let on licence for the grazing of ponies and there is no formal organised sport. Wikipedia gives 103 hectares (254 acres) for the park with Barn Hill Open Space together. It is a nature reserve, classed as Metropolitan Open Land and as a wildlife site of Metropolitan Importance under the system Brent and the Greater London Authority use, and it carries no entry on the National Heritage List for England.

places.name: Sudbury Town Underground Station
places.address: Sudbury Town Underground Station, Station Approach, Sudbury, Wembley HA0 2LA
places.summary: Sudbury Town Underground Station, on Station Approach, HA0 2LA, is listed Grade II*, NHLE 1294594, on 19 February 1971. It is a working station on the Uxbridge branch of the Piccadilly line, between Sudbury Hill and Alperton, in fare zone 4, and the ticket hall can be seen without admission. The forecourt is known as Station Crescent, and Sudbury & Harrow Road on Chiltern Railways is 491 m away.
places.history: Wikidata holds the station as Q1768993 and gives Charles Holden as the architect. The National Heritage List for England records eight Grade II* entries inside the Brent boundary and this is one of them, while Brent Council states nine for the borough. The main entrance on Station Approach is in Brent, on the boundary the station shares with Ealing. A K8 telephone kiosk at Northwick Park station is listed Grade II, NHLE 1485378, on 9 June 2023.

places.name: Barham Park
places.address: Barham Park, 660 Harrow Road, Wembley HA0 2HB
places.summary: Barham Park, at 660 Harrow Road, HA0 2HB, is free and managed by Brent Council, with free parking on site for about 16 cars. The council describes a gently undulating park with pathways and many mature trees that has maintained much of its formal Victorian character, and calls the walled garden a popular relaxation spot with visitors; a dog control order applies to the walled garden. Sudbury Town Underground station is 354 m away and Sudbury & Harrow Road 408 m.
places.history: The park and several local landmarks take their name from the Barham family, formerly major landowners in Sudbury. The surviving structures of Barham Old Court - garden walls, gates, a pergola of two Portland stone Ionic columns and a sundial on Portland stone Ionic columns - are listed Grade II, NHLE 1294729, on 15 March 1979, while the park itself is not on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens. Wembley Fire Station, on Harrow Road, is listed Grade II, NHLE 1247236, on 24 November 2000, and the Grade II* Hundred Elms Farm outbuilding, NHLE 1078876, listed 6 October 1952, stands 1,087 m north-west at Dyson Court, HA0 2NZ.

links.note: Queen's Park is the park in Brent and the ward name in Westminster, and Paddington Old Cemetery carries a Westminster parish's name on Willesden Lane.
Brent Reservoir, the Welsh Harp, is one sheet of water straddling the Brent-Barnet boundary, fed by the Silk Stream and the River Brent.
Sudbury Town, NHLE 1294594, stands on the Brent-Ealing line; Charles Holden designed it and Acton Town in Ealing on one Piccadilly programme.
Kilburn High Road is the Brent-Camden boundary: the Gaumont State Cinema and Kiln Theatre stand on the Brent side, the West Hampstead stations in Camden.

entries.name: Wembley Stadium
entries.note: A 90,000-seat ground of 2007 under a 134-metre arch, entered on event days by ticket and otherwise by booked stadium tour.

entries.name: OVO Arena Wembley
entries.note: The Empire Pool of July 1934, listed Grade II as NHLE 1078877, holding 12,500 and admitting ticket holders to events only.

entries.name: Brent Town Hall
entries.note: Listed Grade II as NHLE 1262141 on 24 September 1990; a school occupies it, and the long facade is seen from Forty Lane.

entries.name: Gaumont State Cinema
entries.note: Listed Grade II* as NHLE 1078889, by George Coles, seating 4,004, with a 120 ft tower modelled on the Empire State Building.

entries.name: Kiln Theatre
entries.note: A producing theatre at 269 Kilburn High Road in a Foresters' hall of 1929, converted in 1980 and renamed Kiln in September 2018.

entries.name: Queen's Park
entries.note: Thirty acres run by the City of London Corporation, with an 1891 Macfarlane bandstand listed Grade II as NHLE 1382063 and a cafe.

entries.name: Paddington Old Cemetery
entries.note: A Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1001542, opened 1855, with month-by-month hours and chapels listed as NHLE 1359002.

entries.name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
entries.note: A stone mandir of 1995 on Brentfield Road, open 9.00am to 6.00pm year-round, with free entry and an exhibition on Hinduism.

entries.name: St Mary's Church, Willesden
entries.note: Listed Grade II* as NHLE 1359036; a church has stood here since 938 and the present building dates from the 13th century.

entries.name: Willesden Jewish Cemetery
entries.note: A Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1449184, in use since 1873, with a heritage centre opened to visitors in September 2020.

entries.name: Roundwood Park
entries.note: A Grade II registered park and garden, NHLE 1001556, of 10.63 hectares, with an aviary, a cafe and bowling greens taken by booking.

entries.name: Brent Museum and Archives
entries.note: The borough museum and record office on the second floor of the Willesden Green library, free, open seven days with narrower archive hours.

entries.name: Church of All Souls, Harlesden
entries.note: Listed Grade II* as NHLE 1359000 on 23 January 1974, on the traffic island where Station Road meets Harlesden High Street.

entries.name: Old St Andrew's Church, Kingsbury
entries.note: Listed Grade I as NHLE 1188676; the Churches Conservation Trust admits visitors by appointment only, so arrange access before travelling.

entries.name: Brent Reservoir (the Welsh Harp)
entries.note: Open water and marsh straddling the Brent-Barnet boundary, owned by the Canal & River Trust, with free access to towpaths from Birchen Grove.

entries.name: Fryent Country Park
entries.note: 103 hectares of Middlesex countryside on the Capital Ring, with Barn Hill at 86 m and Kingsbury station 539 m from Fryent Way.

entries.name: Sudbury Town Underground Station
entries.note: Charles Holden's Piccadilly line station, listed Grade II* as NHLE 1294594; the ticket hall can be seen without admission.

entries.name: Barham Park
entries.note: A Victorian park with a walled garden, 354 m from Sudbury Town, where Barham Old Court's walls and pergola are listed as NHLE 1294729.
